name: Mantling Rime
description: Mantling Rime is a small ice world wrapped in a shell of frost so thick and uniform that the planet appears shrouded in a white cloak from orbit. The surface ice is layered, with strata of water ice, carbon dioxide ice, and methane ice creating a geological record readable in the walls of the few crevasses that breach the mantle. Geothermal vents in the southern hemisphere keep patches of subsurface ocean liquid, and these warm zones support the planet's only known life.

The surface is a study in white and grey, with the thin atmosphere providing just enough haze to soften the harsh shadows of the low sun. The frozen methane lakes are treacherous, their surfaces appearing solid but concealing pockets of slush that can swallow equipment without warning. Sound is muffled and strange in the cold thin air, words falling flat a few meters from the speaker and silence rushing in to fill the gap.

Ancient ruins extend beneath the ice in the geothermal zone, their architecture preserved in perfect frozen detail where the structures intersect the ice layer. The ruins predate the current ice age by an estimated fifty thousand years, suggesting they were built when the planet was warmer and more hospitable. The microbial life in the subsurface ocean clusters around the ruins' foundations, feeding on mineral deposits that may have been placed there intentionally as a biological support system.

Mantling Rime's endangered microbes are genetically distinct from all other known extremophiles, making their preservation a scientific priority. The ruins offer a rare opportunity to study a civilization that adapted to or anticipated catastrophic climate change, and their relationship with the microbial ecosystem suggests sophisticated bioengineering. The geothermal vents that sustain both the microbes and the liquid ocean are weakening measurably, and models predict the ocean will freeze solid within centuries, taking the microbes and whatever secrets the ruins hold with it.
